I set up the Go module with gocheck (`gopkg.in/check.v1`) and an example package whose test suite uses fixtures and all four setup/teardown hooks. Vet is clean and all 3 tests pass. The benchmark also runs. I haven't committed anything.

**Files created in `/work`:**
- `go.mod` / `go.sum`: the module is `example.com/project` (Go 1.27.1), with `gopkg.in/check.v1` as its dependency.
- `stack/stack.go`: a small LIFO stack, just there to have something to test.
- `stack/stack_test.go`: an example gocheck suite that shows:
  - `func Test(t *testing.T) { TestingT(t) }`, which connects gocheck to `go test`. You only need one of these per package.
  - `var _ = Suite(&StackSuite{})`, which registers the suite. Its fields hold the shared fixtures.
  - `SetUpSuite` / `TearDownSuite`, which run once per suite. The example creates a fixture file in `c.MkDir()`, a temp directory gocheck deletes automatically.
  - `SetUpTest` / `TearDownTest`, which run before and after each test to give it a fresh stack.
  - `c.Assert` (stops the test on failure) and `c.Check` (records the failure and keeps going), with the `IsNil` and `Equals` checkers.
  - A `Benchmark*` method that uses `c.N`.
- `.gitignore`: ignores test binaries and coverage output.

**Commands:**
```sh
go test ./...                              # run all suites
go test ./stack -check.v                   # verbose, per-test output
go test ./stack -check.f 'TestPop.*'       # filter tests by regex
go test ./stack -check.b                   # run benchmarks
```

`example.com/project` is a placeholder module path. To use your real repo path, change it with `go mod edit -module github.com/you/project`.
